draft.title: Controlled and extraneous variables
card: Extraneous variable
any variable other than the independent variable that could affect the dependent variable and change the results.
Controlled variable
an extraneous variable the researcher keeps the same for all participants, so that only the independent variable changes.
Confounding variable
an extraneous variable that has affected the dependent variable, so the researcher cannot tell whether the result came from it or the independent variable.
Researchers try to spot extraneous variables early and control them, to lower the chance of confounding.
draft.remember: Extraneous could affect results. Controlled is kept the same. Confounding already has.

a.q: Why do researchers keep the room temperature the same for every participant in a reaction time study?
opts: So temperature is less likely to affect the results
So the independent variable is measured, not changed
So the hypothesis is written before data are collected
So every participant belongs to the same population
a.why: Temperature is an extraneous variable, and keeping it the same makes it a controlled variable. Any difference in reaction time is then more likely due to the independent variable.
a.clue: What does keeping something the same stop it from doing?

b.q: Leo tests a revision app. The app group studies in the morning and the no-app group studies at night. The app group scores higher. What is time of day?
opts: A confounding variable, as it may have affected the scores
A controlled variable, as it was the same for both groups
The independent variable, as the researcher changed it
The dependent variable, as the researcher measured it
b.why: Time of day differed between the groups and could have affected scores, so it may have already influenced the results. That makes it confounding. It was not kept the same, so it is not controlled.
b.clue: Was time of day the same for both groups?

a.best: So temperature is less likely to affect the results

b.best: A confounding variable, as it may have affected the scores

problems.detail: The card and remember line define a confounding variable as one that 'has affected' the results ('Confounding already has'), with 'could affect' marking a merely extraneous variable. The right option and the why say time of day 'may have affected' the scores. A careful student using the card's wording could read that as extraneous rather than confounding. Rewording the option to say time of day differed between the groups, so the effect of the app cannot be separated from it, would match the card.

check.summary: Both questions have one clearly right answer and the facts are correct. The only issue is that question b's right option and why say confounding 'may have affected' the scores, while the card says a confounding variable 'has affected' them, which blurs the line the card draws with extraneous variables.
